readingRule.method: Pixel lint takes each visible glyph's centre and the two ends of its advance from the renderer's own text-animator poses (prepared layout), through the layer matrix. A reading run continues while every point moves <= velocity letter-heights/s, has travelled <= displacement letter-heights since the run began, and has not turned > 90 degrees from its first direction in the run (steps < 0.1 px carry no direction). Glyph blur > 0.5 px or glyph opacity below reading opacity end a run. The words-per-second requirement is unchanged. Without glyph evidence (state lint, system fonts) the layer corners are followed with letter = 0.7 font size and any text-animator change still ends a run.
readingRule.calibration: Proof T1-T3 holds (tracking +25/+30, a 14 px rise) peak at 0.16-0.88 letter-heights/s with <= 0.52 of travel on the real treatments; fast (600 px, ~4/s), jitter (+/-1 px) and spin (360 degrees) holds end runs on speed, reversal and speed. Velocity is the owner's own figure (1 letter-height/s); displacement 2 letter-heights lets a heading (1 s) use the full speed and shortens allowed speed for longer reading (a 3 s body line may move <= 0.67/s).

treatedEdgeContrast.why: ET3 compares each glyph pixel with the frame behind it: an outline ring counts as glyph and shadows and halos get no credit, so treated display text measured 1.0-1.9:1 while it read well.
treatedEdgeContrast.method: The glyph mask draws the fill in word codes and the text-animator outline in a ring code (#00ff00). Fill edge: at each fill pixel on a letter edge, mean linear luminance of the fill in a window vs every non-fill, non-anti-aliased pixel in the window (outline, halo, shadow or footage), as rendered. Outer edge: at each outline pixel on the ring's outside, the outlined letter (fill + ring) vs the pixels outside. Window half-size round(width/reviewWidth)+1 px (one review pixel past the anti-aliased edge), so a ring thinner than a phone pixel blends with the footage. Each edge's value is a percentile of its pixels; a word takes the better edge. Text layers stacked above the measured one are drawn as occluders (#0000ff) and left out, with edges against them. Hollow (outline-only) text, which samples treat as invisible, gets a reading window by its outline. No background render is needed.
treatedEdgeContrast.occluders: Found on a01: 'IT' read 1.38 because the script 'layer' above it covers part of it with a cream outline; with occluders 17.39, matching 'UP'.

percentileCalibration.finding: At the 5th percentile two accepted words fall below untreated text: a02 '&' (crimson over a black top; it reads by hue, which luminance cannot see) 1.04 and a06 'SUNDAY' (cream hollow outline, 'Y' over a cream lace sleeve) 1.14, against 1.23 for untreated or hairline-outlined white display text over matching footage. No level can pass all 16 and fail untreated text at the 5th or 25th percentile; at the median the accepted minimum is 1.63 and the untreated fixtures stay 1.23.
percentileCalibration.choice: Display text is measured at the median of each word's edge (a large word reads when most of its edge is clear); small text keeps ET3's 5th percentile.

sizeSplit.decision: ET3-D1 (G1): display text may go below 3:1; small text keeps 4.5:1.
sizeSplit.boundary: 24 px font size at the 360 px review width (WCAG's large-text size; 48 px at 720, 72 px at 1080), using the layer's smallest span size at its smallest layer scale over the reading frames. On the pilot it separates every boxed label (12-23 px) from every heading (28-130 px).

knownLimits: WCAG luminance cannot credit hue contrast (a02's crimson '&' over black).
Fully invisible text (transparent fill, no outline) has no reading window and is not reported.
The reading rule needs pixel lint to see text-animator motion; state lint keeps the default text-clock rule for it.
Declared reading windows and speech captions keep their own rules.
Occluders are root text layers only; shapes, images and decorations stacked above are not.

profile.surface: 720x1280 Canvas layer surface, one 400x200 opaque block, blur 16 (kernel radius 48)
profile.method: Node micro-benchmark of the exported shadow-effects steps

ec.cause: The Canvas light.drop-shadow kernel ran bilinear mask sampling, two Gaussian passes and a per-pixel composite over every pixel of the layer surface in JavaScript, about 0.6 s per 720x1280 frame per shadowed layer. Lint paid it again for the legibility background probe, whose glyphs are transparent (all-zero work).
ec.fix: Outer shadows compute only inside the painted pixels' bounds shifted by the offset, widened by one sample step and by the kernel radius per pass; every other pixel keeps the exact premultiply round trip. Inner shadows keep the full surface. Pixels byte-identical; renderer versions unchanged.
ec.failingFirst: tests/unit/composition-shadow-region.test.ts: a 16 px glyph on a 2048x2048 surface took 2.45 s on main (bound 1.5 s); byte identity against the full-surface oracle in six cases.
ec.candidates: All 16 MP4 render SHA-256s are identical to Phase 1's corrected renders (list under et6b.candidates.list). Timings are four candidates at a time on one machine, so contention adds noise; the shadowed ones fell most (a03 154.5 -> 19.6 s render, 420.6 -> 18.9 s lint; a07 226.8 -> 41.9 s, 490.8 -> 39.5 s). Lint also changed method (treated-edge needs no background render).
notChanged: light.glow: its blur is the browser's own filter; fixture 6.8-11.1 s across runs vs 6.2-6.5 s untreated.
WebGL2 drop shadow: GPU passes, not the reported cost.
Inner shadows: full surface by nature.
